claim: Reported (not found on an OpenAI page) cut to the $200 ChatGPT Pro plan: from Oct 30, 2026 included ChatGPT Work/Codex usage falls from 20x to 10x Plus, and weekly GPT-6 Pro messages in Chat drop from 200 to 100. Existing $200 subscribers keep current limits through Oct 29.
quote: included usage in ChatGPT Work and Codex drops from 20x to 10x the Plus allowance

claim: OpenAI paused new sign-ups for the $200 Pro plan on Sept 10, 2026, citing strain from GPT-6 Astra demand. Existing subscribers were unaffected. Sottiaux announced it on X.
quote: We wanted to take the smallest step that allows us to continue giving the broadest access possible.

topic: OpenAI: Pro $200 reopening at half usage
claim: OpenAI reopened the $200 Pro plan to new subscribers on Sept 29-30, 2026 at the same price with smaller usage. Sottiaux said it nets out to half the API-dollar value of the old plan. Multiples vs Plus are now Pro $100 = 5x and Pro $200 = 10x (previously 20x). Existing $200 subscribers keep 20x for a while and get extra credits (amount unpublished).
quote: Tomorrow we are re-opening the Pro $200 subscriptions to new subscribers.

claim: OpenAI announced a $500/month ChatGPT Pro 500 plan at DevDay on Sept 29, 2026. It offers 25x Plus usage and the 'Ultrafast' GPT-6 Astra setting, which the $200 plan does not get. Cited to OpenAI Help Center 'ChatGPT Work and Codex'; the page I fetched relayed it second-hand.
quote: Ultrafast is available to Pro $500 subscribers and eligible Enterprise and Edu workspaces.

claim: OpenAI brought back the 5-hour usage limit on Codex and ChatGPT Work for Plus on Aug 25, 2026, after several weeks with only a weekly cap. It stays off for Pro $100 and Pro $200 'for the upcoming months'. Sottiaux gave load smoothing as the reason.
quote: Tomorrow we will bring back the 5h limit for Plus accounts across ChatGPT Work and Codex.

claim: OpenAI introduced a $100/month Pro tier on Apr 9, 2026, with 5x Plus Codex usage. It said the temporary extra Codex access for Plus was ending. Plus stays $20/month; the $200 Pro was described as 20x Plus at that time.
quote: This new tier offers 5x more Codex usage than Plus and is best for longer, high-effort Codex sessions.

claim: OpenAI launched GPT-6 Sol and Luna on Sept 22, 2026 at 50% lower API prices. Sol went from $4/$20 to $2/$10 per million tokens; Luna from $0.20/$1.20 to $0.10/$0.50. The baseline is GPT-5.6 promotional pricing.
quote: They are also half the price per token, and even less per task.

claim: Anthropic's launch post (Sept 22, 2026) gives Opus 5.5 at $4 input / $20 output per million tokens versus $5/$25 for Opus 5. That is 20% lower per token. Cache reads fall 60% ($0.50 to $0.20). Anthropic separately claims about 40% lower cost on typical workloads at default settings, which includes lower token use per task.
quote: Opus 5.5 costs 40% less than Opus 5 on typical workloads

claim: Anthropic's pricing page lists Opus 5.5 at $4/$20 per million tokens. Opus 5, 4.8, 4.7, 4.6 and 4.5 are all $5/$25. Opus 4.1 (retired) was $15/$75. Sonnet 5.5 and Sonnet 5 are $2/$10, and Fable 5.1 is $10/$50.
The $2/$10 introductory price for Sonnet 5 became the standard price. The scheduled Sept 1, 2026 increase to $3/$15 will not occur.
The Opus 5.5 launch post says five-hour usage limits increase on Pro, Max, Team and seat-based Enterprise plans, with no numbers given. Subscribers also get a saveable rate-limit reset.

Anthropic announced weekly limits on Jul 28, 2025, effective Aug 28, 2025 for Pro ($20) and Max ($100/$200). Anthropic said they would affect fewer than 5% of subscribers. Anthropic cited 24/7 background Claude Code use, account sharing and reselling.

Max 5x is $100/month and Max 20x is $200/month. They give 5x and 20x Pro's per-session usage, plus a weekly limit across all models. Claude.com/pricing shows Pro at $20 monthly, or $17/month billed annually. Prices are unchanged at $20/$100/$200.
source: Anthropic Help Center, What is the Max plan? (fetched 2026-10-27)
quote: Max plans also have a weekly usage limit that applies across all models.

claim: Claude.com/pricing says Max 5x and Max 20x get 50% of weekly limits for the Fable model, while Pro uses usage credits. The Claude Code help page says Max also has a separate weekly Fable limit. The Max help page does not mention it.

On May 6, 2026 Anthropic doubled Claude Code's five-hour rate limits for Pro, Max, Team and seat-based Enterprise. It also removed the peak-hours reduction on Pro and Max. It tied this to new compute, including all of SpaceX's Colossus 1 (more than 300 MW).
quote: doubling Claude Code's five-hour rate limits for Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans

topic: Anthropic: weekly boost and net 17% cut
claim: Anthropic announced a permanent 25% increase to standard Claude Code weekly limits starting Sept 14, 2026. This replaced a temporary 50% boost that had been in place since May 13. Against the boosted level that is a 17% net cut. Anthropic deleted the original post and acknowledged the 17% figure.
quote: Compared to today, this works out to a 17% reduction in weekly limits on Claude Code.

claim: On Apr 14, 2026 GIGAZINE reported Max 5x users hitting quota in about 1.5 hours. It said Anthropic had announced tighter usage limits to manage load, with no exact date. A promo of doubled 5-hour limits off-peak ran Mar 13-28, 2026, per a secondary blog.

A proposed class action was reportedly filed Jun 14, 2026 (N.D. Cal., No. 3:26-cv-05763). It alleges Max 5x delivers about 3.5x Pro and Max 20x delivers 6-8x Pro. The page gives no docket link, and Anthropic reportedly moved to dismiss on Aug 19 with a hearing set for Nov 6, 2026. I could not verify this against the docket or an outlet.

SemiAnalysis reportedly (Jun 2026) bought every plan and ran coding agents until weekly limits ran out. A full $200 ChatGPT Pro is worth about $14,000/month at API prices and a Claude Max 20x about $8,000. These are API-equivalent values, not measured provider costs. OpenAI margins reportedly turn negative above 11.4% utilization on Plus/Pro 5x; Anthropic's breakpoint is about 20%. I did not read the SemiAnalysis original.
quote: cost OpenAI roughly $14,000 per month in API-equivalent compute

claim: In Jan 2025 Altman said OpenAI was losing money on the $200 Pro plan because people used it more than expected. This is 2025 evidence, not 2026.

A Jul 2025 newsletter estimated Pro/Max heavy users consumed 200% to 3,000% of their monthly payment in compute, based on self-selected ccusage dashboards that price at public API rates. It says this is not Anthropic data.
quote: CCusage is not direct information from Anthropic

topic: Subsidy: OpenAI cut plan allowance as demand spiked
claim: OpenAI halved the API-dollar value of the $200 plan while saying the $500 tier concentrates the highest usage. This is consistent with a subsidised plan being rationed, but OpenAI has not disclosed its cost per task. The OfficeChai article says the company is rationing 'through plan design rather than only through rate limits'.
quote: the company is rationing access through plan design rather than only through rate limits
